calls.reason: Nye et al. (2021) found unaided GPT-3 answered only 29% of bAbI state-tracking questions and could not keep stories coherent, while Gopher showed substantial factual knowledge in the same period.
This is a judgment about scientific explanation plus a contested description of what models learn. The GPT-3 and RAVEN papers give context only, and there is no agreed test.

The Gopher paper and DeepMind's announcement report gains from scale but little benefit on logical reasoning and common-sense tasks, which stayed well below human level. PaLM's gains don't negate 'some measures'.
Evidence is mixed. Mishra et al. show uneven but real GPT-3 generalization from instructions, and the T5 study shows some transfer, so a lack of genuine abstraction is not clearly established.

TruthfulQA (best model 58% truthful vs 94% for humans), InstructGPT's made-up facts in 21% vs GPT-3's 41% of outputs, and GPT-3's failure to keep bAbI stories consistent all show recurring truth and coherence failures.

Razeghi et al. link accuracy to how often numbers appear in training data, not to seen versus unseen problems, and decline a causal reading. The earlier GPT-3 paper found few memorised problems, so the evidence is mixed.
